title: The challenge
notes: Businesses are constantly striving to improve decision-making and streamline operations. But today’s data landscape is fragmented, with information spread across countless systems, flowing in real time, and rarely speaking the same language across teams. As a result, connection is lost, and meaning breaks down. Understanding what the data actually means is now the next major challenge. 4

title: Data powers AI
body: Data powers AI But that alone isn’t enough Shared understanding, meaning, and business connection makes it intelligent | 5 | Microsoft Fabric
notes: Every organization wants to make smarter decisions and improve how it operates. The problem isn’t data scarcity – there’s more data than ever before. The real challenge is that this data is scattered across systems, tools, and teams, constantly changing, and rarely connected by a shared understanding. Without common meaning, every team interprets data in its own way. Insights fragment, decisions drift, and the organization loses alignment. title: Without shared context, every team has a different view
body: When “active plane” means something different to everyone: Maintenance sees it as “not in the hangar” Operations sees it as “assigned to a flight” Leadership asks, “How many active planes do we have?” – and gets conflicting answers | The result: Fragmented views lead to misalignment, slowing decisions and blocking effective action. | 8 | Microsoft Fabric
notes: This challenge becomes clear at the individual team level. Without shared context, each group interprets data in its own way. For maintenance, an “active plane” means it’s in the hangar. For operations, it means the plane is currently flying. And when leadership asks how many active planes they have, every team gives a different answer. They’re all looking at valid data, but none of it connects. Meaning gets lost between teams, and what should be one shared reality becomes a set of conflicting truths. And when every team is working from its own version of the truth, those gaps ripple upward...

title: Most AI only sees snapshots – but work happens in context
body: AI today | How work actually happens | Chat | Context gap | New priority | Email | File | Business Change | Updated information | Task update | Meeting | People | Continuous, evolving, connected | Connectors see fragments of data
notes: Work unfolds across chats, meetings, files, org changes, and decisions over time. . AI is increasingly expected to help teams keep up — but most AI today doesn’t see work the way people do. It sees moments, not motion. This is because it works from snapshots: a prompt, a document, a transcript fragment. But work context lives across time and systems, And when you can’t see past all those fragments - you create a context gap. AI fills in the gap by guessing — owners, dependencies, what changed, and what’s next. The real opportunity is AI that can follow work as it’s happening in real-time. 23

notes: Copilot Cowork brings long‑running, multi‑step work into M365 Copilot, moving beyond prompts and responses toward execution that unfolds over time. And, with Work IQ, it has the full context of your work, not just fragments of data, so it can reason over all relevant materials. Instead of asking Copilot to generate a single artifact, Cowork allows you to delegate meaningful work and stay in the loop as that work progresses. With Cowork, Copilot can break down complex requests into steps, reason across tools and files, and carry work forward with visible progress and opportunities to steer. ...
